To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) sentences containing locative indefinitives can have non-existential interpretations, (ii) this is not a matter of decomposing far into its negated antonym and (iii) this is not restricted to non-projective locatives.
(a) locative indefinties are not always interpreted as existentials, and (b) this is due to the fact that they denote properties.

(a) locative indefinites can be used to express false statements, (b) the non-existential reading of such sentences can be explained by the fact that the locative indefinite denotes a property rather than an individual, (c) the property in question is associated with an eigenspace.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what the semantic contribution of indefinites is, and what the nature of the semantic contribution is of the locative determiners they combine with.
a general question: What is the meaning of indefinites?
the semantic representation of indefinites and the relation between the semantics of definite and indefinite descriptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
locative indefinitives are not existential.
the locative indefinite in (1) denotes the property of being far from a gas station.
locative definites and indefinites are ambiguous between a spatial and a locative reading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the existential reading of indefinites is a derived phenomenon.
locatives are not existential quantifiers, but rather properties.
we are far from the gas station.
The main takeaway from our work is that
locative indefinites can give a false reading, and we argue that they are best understood as denoting properties.
theories of indefinites should be based on the properties denoted by indefinites and not on existential quantifiers.

eigenspace semantics can explain the existence of non-existential interpretations of indefinites, and it can do so with greater explanatory power and fewer theoretical assumptions than decomposition into negated adjectives.
